# dsh-task-progress-tab
A **Task Progress** tab for the DeepSeek Harness conversation view. It sits right after the built-in
**Context** tab and turns the session's task list into a live progress view: one bar for the whole
session, completed items numbered in the order they were finished, open items in the order the model
eted items numbered in the order they were finished, open items in the order the model planned them.
## Features

- **Live progress bar** — done / total plus a percentage, updated as the model ticks items off.
- **
Completion order** — completed items are numbered `#1`, `#2`, … in the order they actually finished,

even if the model reorders its plan or the list is regenerated.
- **Open items** — rendered in plan

order, with `in progress` highlighted and `pending` dimmed.
- **Per-session memory** — the todo pro
jection is cleared at the start of every turn; the tab caches each session's last known list so the

view doesn't flash empty between turns.
- **Bilingual** — follows the browser/desktop language (Chin

ese and English are built in).
- **Zero dependencies** — one client bundle, no runtime packages, no

lish are built in).
- **Zero dependencies** — one client bundle, no runtime packages, no build step.

The conversation tab strip becomes:

It registers as a `conversation.view` slot with `order: 40`, so it always lands immediately to the r
ight of the Context tab (which uses `order: 30`).
## How it works
The tab reads the session projection `todos`, which the `todo_write` tool maintains:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Completion order is remembered per session by assigning a monotonic sequence number the first time a
n item is seen as completed. Nothing is written back — the plugin is read-only.
## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.0** or newer (`engines.dsh`), client platform `web`.
- Desktop and browser
(web) builds are both supported; the same client bundle is served for either.

ration metadata, counts, percentages, completion-order stability across reshuffles, the empty state,
the per-session fallback, and both locales.
